_description: Published hotel price elasticity coefficients used as ground truth for the archetype elasticity backtest. Values synthesized from peer-reviewed research on Spanish/Mediterranean resort hotels plus international industry references. These are the academic anchor against which our simulated archetype elasticities are compared.
_methodology: For each simulated archetype we map to the closest published segment and adopt its reported elasticity (own-price, short-run) as the benchmark. Where a range is published we use the midpoint. A confidence class is attached to each anchor.

vives_jacob_2023.label: Vives & Jacob (2023) — Sources of price elasticity variability among Spanish resort hotels. Emerald JHTT.
vives_jacob_2023.sample: 7 four-star Spanish resort hotels, multi-region incl. Balearics & Tenerife

vives_jacob_2021_dynamic.label: Vives & Jacob (2021) — Dynamic pricing in Spanish resort hotels. SAGE Tourism Economics.

garin_munoz_german_spain.label: Garín-Muñoz — German demand for tourism in Spain. Academia.edu pre-print.
garin_munoz_german_spain.finding: German short-run price elasticity to Spain = -1.06; long-run = -2.16

singh_corsun_2023.label: Singh & Corsun (2023) — Price elasticity of demand and its impact on hotel revenue performance during COVID-19. Cornell Hospitality Quarterly.
singh_corsun_2023.note: Full paper paywalled; cited qualitative finding that luxury segment remained inelastic while mid/economy became more elastic during recovery.

xuan_tran_2011_luxury_us.label: Xuan Tran (2011) — Price Sensitivity of Customers in Luxurious Hotels in U.S. e-Review of Tourism Research.
xuan_tran_2011_luxury_us.finding: Luxury hotel demand is price-inelastic; income-elastic

rateboard_industry_consensus.label: Rateboard industry review — hotel price elasticity by segment.
rateboard_industry_consensus.finding: Leisure traveler average PED ≈ -1.23; business ≈ -0.7; luxury ≈ -0.4 to -0.6

hoteltechreport_2024.label: Hotel Tech Report (2024) — Price elasticity in the hotel industry.

archetype_benchmark_elasticity._unit: own-price elasticity of demand (short-run), negative values mean higher price → fewer bookings
archetype_benchmark_elasticity._description: Tolerance is ±0.35 around the midpoint; a sim-produced elasticity within the band counts as a MATCH for that archetype.

luxury_seeker.mapping_note: Luxury hotel demand is consistently reported as inelastic in published research. Value midpoint of -0.30 to -0.60 range.

honeymooner.mapping_note: Couple/honeymoon leisure sits between pure luxury (inelastic) and general leisure (-1.23). Vives notes couple/half-board targeting makes demand more inelastic.

family_vacationer.mapping_note: Families display lower price elasticity than solo travelers (-1.008 reported in Spanish resort study).

business_traveler.mapping_note: Business travel is inelastic; bookings charged to corporate budgets, price-insensitive up to policy ceiling.

digital_nomad.mapping_note: Similar to general leisure (-1.23) with slight extra sensitivity due to longer stays and self-funded.

budget_optimizer.mapping_note: Solo travelers: -1.574 reported. Budget optimizer is a more extreme case of solo price-sensitivity.

loyalty_maximizer.primary_source: Industry synthesis — loyalty members absorb price via points
loyalty_maximizer.mapping_note: Loyalty program members are less price-sensitive because points/upgrades offset rate variability.

event_attendee.primary_source: Industry consensus + event hotel pricing literature
event_attendee.mapping_note: Event-constrained dates/locations; mildly more elastic than leisure since alternatives exist within event city.

cluster_modifier_benchmark._description: Cultural cluster modifiers applied on top of archetype elasticity — additive to archetype value.

german_dach.source: garin_munoz_german_spain (short-run -1.06 vs industry leisure avg -1.23 = -0.35 relative Hmm wait this means less elastic... let me recheck)
german_dach.note: Actually German short-run to Spain (-1.06) is less elastic than leisure avg (-1.23), so modifier is +0.17 (less elastic). Correcting.

cluster_modifier_benchmark_corrected._description: Corrected cultural modifier — positive values mean less elastic (more price-tolerant). Based on published origin-market differences.

german_dach.interpretation: Germans to Spain short-run: -1.06 vs industry leisure avg -1.23. Modifier +0.17 = less elastic.

anglo_uk_ireland.interpretation: UK to Mediterranean: baseline, matches industry leisure avg.

latin_spain_italy.interpretation: Domestic Spain/Italy leisure: price-fluid, experience-driven. +0.15 less elastic.

french.interpretation: French leisure to Mediterranean: marginally less elastic than UK baseline.

nordic.interpretation: Nordic: affluent leisure, price-tolerant for warm-destination exception.

anglo_us_canada.interpretation: US/Canada long-haul leisure to Europe: less elastic due to trip premium.
